cues: Only two place names appear, a few hundred metres apart.
Thamel is the tourist quarter, Kathmandu's brightest and richest street.
Kesharmahal is a Rana palace with the Kaiser Library and the Garden of Dreams, and old trees where fruit bats really roost.
So homeless children cry with hunger under the bat bearing trees of a palace full of books and a garden built for pleasure.
Subedi does not point it out.
He puts the two things in one sentence and lets you do the arithmetic.
